6671ea6c9954a449: KUALA LUMPUR: Hundreds of children gathered in Klang recently to build catapults, solve mysteries, conduct experiments, and even try their hands at being doctors and police detectives for a day.
Behind all the fun was a bigger purpose: helping underprivileged children discover their strengths, build confidence and imagine what they might become.

Held on Aug 22 at Andalas Sports Complex, the Hope2Kids Soft Skills & Career Aspirations Camp brought together 507 children from 16 shelter homes and informal learning centres across the Klang Valley.
The event earned Hope2Kids a place in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBR) for “Most Underprivileged Children Participants in a Career Aspirations Camp”.

Founded in January 2025, Hope2Kids is a youth-led non-profit that works with children from orphanages and refugee centres through self-discovery workshops, career-immersion experiences and soft-skills training.

Prior to this, the organisation had mainly organised smaller programmes at individual shelter homes and centres. Founder Sarah Callista Ng had long envisioned something bigger that could bring children from different backgrounds together under one roof.

“We wanted to give them a day where they could develop their soft skills and teamwork, explore potential career aspirations, and form new friendships while simply enjoying being children together,” Ng, 19, told FMT Lifestyle.
Ng was one of three Malaysians selected to receive the Queen Elizabeth II Commonwealth Trust Young Leaders Award this year in recognition of their efforts in driving meaningful social change.
Throughout the camp, participants tackled activities designed to develop communication, teamwork, leadership, creativity and critical thinking.

In “Operation Lost Explorer”, blindfolded kids navigated an obstacle course using only their teammates’ verbal instructions, while “Project Hungry Zoo” challenged them to design, build and test their own catapults.

For 13-year-old Kirina from Noble Education Centre, the catapult challenge proved particularly meaningful. “I have always wanted to be an engineer. After the camp, I feel more confident in my engineering skills,” she said.
“Building and designing a working catapult showed me that I can use my ideas to create something that actually works, which made me even more excited to become an engineer in the future.”
Another major attraction was the Career Marketplace, featuring 35 interactive stations across five career themes.

The children became junior doctors assessing patients, police detectives cracking cases, and scientists conducting experiments. Budding entrepreneurs created and marketed their own products, while young archaeologists deciphered clues in search of lost treasure.
For some participants, those playful simulations opened the door to new possibilities.
Ng spoke of one girl who had always dreamed of becoming an astronaut but, after taking part in the doctor station, decided she instead wanted to become a doctor and help people lead healthier lives.

The day was also about making connections: Ng fondly recalled four girls from different homes who became friends during the camp. For another young participant, meeting children with similar experiences reminded him that he was not alone.

Ultimately, Ng hopes the children discovered something new about themselves through the camp - a potential career path, greater confidence in their abilities, stronger teamwork skills, or simply a greater sense of belong.
Ng also hopes there will be future editions, with even more careers and hands-on experiences for young ones to explore.
“We want to continue to give children the opportunity for self-discovery, help them discover their career interests and dream big,” she concluded.
Find out more about Hope2Kids here.

8b0b7167951d3876: PONTIANAK: Toiling around the clock, haggard Indonesian firefighters on Borneo island cannot keep up with the blazes devouring landscapes and shrouding communities in a cloying haze.
They are fighting a perilous battle with limited weapons against fires blamed in part on a stronger-than-usual episode of the El Nino climate phenomenon parching Southeast Asia.
Experts also blame climate change, decades of forest degradation and slash-and-burn land clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape.
"We are exhausted. Sometimes we carry out firefighting until dawn. Sometimes we don't sleep," said Sampe Ritonga, fire chief for Sintang regency.

"Our facilities and infrastructure for firefighting are very limited," he told AFP, standing on the smouldering embers of a peatland fire separated from a residential settlement by a narrow dirt road.
Behind him, veiled by the haze, the sun appeared as an eerie, rust-coloured ball in the brown-grey sky.
Sampe's team only has two 6,000-litre fire engines, and deploys one at a time while the other refills. They also face a shortage of hoses.
The team has fought dozens of fires this month.
With river levels low, "we look for available water in ditches... (and) small rivers", some far from active burn sites, Sampe said.
"So there are difficulties because they have to first carry out firefighting with high intensity, and second look for water," he added.
"With the limitations we have, we try as hard as we can to extinguish the fires and also to reduce the smoke."
Nearby, locals gathered to observe the team's efforts, offering drinking water to first responders.
"There are many houses here, and that is what we have to protect," said Sampe.
- 'CRACKLING SOUND' -
Resident Sutrismi, 47, said she was at home on Saturday when she heard a "crackling sound", looked out of the window and saw smoke rising from the peatland across the road.
Peatland fires, common in the area, generally smoulder and spread under the soil for weeks or months, emitting huge quantities of smoke and only rarely causing surface blazes.
"First thing, I looked for help. I contacted the village head, asked for assistance," Sutrismi told AFP.
"I am scared. Truly scared."
Some 400km away in Pontianak – the capital of West Kalimantan province – people have been breathing foul air for weeks.
The haze can be smelled even indoors in the city of about 700,000 people.
At one point on Sunday, the level of PM2.5 pollution exceeded 500 micrograms per cubic metre, according to IQAir, a Switzerland-based monitor.

That is more than 100 times the World Health Organization's recommended safe limit for airborne particles so small they can enter deep into the lungs and even the bloodstream, with potentially dire consequences for health.
Hundreds of schools have been closed indefinitely in West Kalimantan due to air pollution, with about 200,000 pupils learning from home, according to the education ministry.
The province has also recorded a surge in respiratory ailments.
"We really hope there will be some assistance or grants for us, so we can be faster, more alert and more responsive," said Sampe.
West Kalimantan governor Ria Norsan said the province was doing its best.
"We do not want officers in the field to work with limitations," he said in a statement to AFP.
"Every report regarding shortages of personnel, equipment, water, or other needs must be conveyed immediately so that solutions can be found."

The provincial government has said it has nearly 14,500 fire-fighting personnel out in the field, with nine aircraft available for water-bombing, three for patrols and one for cloud-seeding operations trying to make rain.
- CLIMATE CONNECTION -
Environmental campaigners say rapacious forest and peatland destruction is the root cause of the fires.
"The peat is drained by extractive plantations, monoculture plantations, whether oil palm or pulpwood," Greenpeace Indonesia forest campaigner Belgis Habiba told AFP in Pontianak.
"When the water is drained, the peat dries and becomes flammable."
According to Greenpeace estimates using government data, some 35 million people in Indonesia are exposed to toxic haze.
Smoke from the fires has also affected communities in the neighbouring Malaysian part of Borneo and beyond.
"The haze is massive and everywhere, and it's actually very unfit for people to breathe," Belgis said.
She urged the Indonesian government to declare the fires a national disaster, "so that all resources are mobilised... to build health access for residents, rescue wildlife and so on."
According to the Nusantara Atlas fire tracker, more than 285,000 hectares have burnt in Indonesia so far this year.
Official data show 38,000 hectares have burnt in West Kalimantan.
The current El Nino event, which will last into next year, is likely to be one of the strongest in decades, according to the United Nations.--AFP

c746111e780aa62c: BARCELONA: Lamine Yamal struck twice for Barcelona as they demolished Valencia 5-0 on Sunday to maintain their 100% start in La Liga.
The reigning champions moved two points clear at the top of La Liga after Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.
Unbeaten Alaves rose to second place with a thumping 5-2 victory over Osasuna.
As well as Yamal, Fermin Lopez, Raphinha and Pedri were also on target for Hansi Flick's swaggering Barca on a hot afternoon on Spain's east coast.
Yamal did not take part in the team training session on Saturday after a knock but showed no signs of it during a dazzling display against Carlos Corberan's side.

Barcelona, the only team in the top flight to win their first four games, took control from the start to the upset of Valencia's fans at a persistently bad-tempered Mestalla stadium. Los Che are bottom and yet to win this season.
"We played a fantastic game, it was nearly perfect, we controlled, we were dominant, and this is what I want from the team," said Flick.
"We stay calm and then if it's possible to score, we try to do it – it was a fantastic game for us.
"Nothing is perfect, you always can improve. If it's perfect, then you can stop working."
Yamal opened the scoring with a clever lofted finish in the sixth minute after Lopez dinked a superb ball over the top for the teenage star.
The 19-year-old slammed home at the near post for what he thought was Barca's second goal but the goal was disallowed for a tight offside after a VAR review.
Lopez netted the second with a crisp finish in the 22nd minute after former Newcastle winger Anthony Gordon teed him up.

Barcelona suffered a blow when Eric Garcia had to go off hurt midway through the first half after a collision with teammate Rodri's shoulder, on the midfielder's first start since arriving this summer from Manchester City.
Yamal fired narrowly wide, and Lopez struck the post as Flick's side continued to dominate. Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia made a smart save to thwart Arnaut Danjuma at his near post before the break.
Raphinha, starting again as the team's centre-forward, tapped home his sixth goal of the season from close range after Lopez fed him.
Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski saved from Rodri before Pedri netted Barcelona's fourth after an exchange of passes with Dani Olmo.
A long way to go
New arrival Gabriel Jesus came on for his Barca debut as a substitute in the final 10 minutes and sent a low effort just wide.
Yamal stayed onside to collect another Olmo pass and put away Barca's fifth and conclude a profitable afternoon for both the World Cup winner and the Catalan giants.

"We have a very young team, with the right transfers we made, but it's the beginning of the season, it's not the end," added Flick, telling his team not to get too excited yet about their strong start.
"We have to go a long, long way."
Corberan said his team were up against it from the start after Yamal's rapid strike.
"Conceding a goal so early, on their first or second attack, made everything much more difficult," said the Valencia coach.
"It's a difficult situation that we will navigate together."
Later on Sunday Lucas Boye bagged a hat-trick for Alaves as they crushed Osasuna 5-2, with two of his efforts coming from long range.
Former Real Madrid striker Mariano Diaz and Pablo Ibanez also scored for Quique Sanchez Flores's team, while Ante Budimir grabbed two for Osasuna, who fell to their first defeat.
"I hope we don't take our foot off the gas and we stay in this dynamic, which will take us far," said Boye.
"This is a humble team and we will go game by game."
df89aef4ca9f2bb2: JAKARTA: About 170,000 passengers were left stranded on Sunday as Indonesia shuttered its main international airport and seven others, cancelling hundreds of flights after Mount Anak Krakatoa spewed a plume of volcanic ash and lava from more than 150 kilometres away.
Mount Anak Krakatoa erupted on Saturday, producing a fountain of lava and booming sounds that could be heard up to a few hundred kilometres away, the geology agency said in a statement.
Two new eruptions were recorded on Sunday, the volcanology agency warned.
Ash from the volcano was detected in the airspace surrounding Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, prompting authorities to suspend operations, the ministry said.
The suspension was extended until 8.59am Monday "due to increased eruptive activity at Mount Anak Krakatoa", the airport authority said in an Instagram post.

Operations were also suspended at seven other airports until 8.59am, authorities said on Instagram. These include the Husein Sastranegara airport in Bandung and Radin Inten II airport near Bandar Lampung on Sumatra, the ministry said.
"To date, 1,558 flights have been delayed at the eight affected airports, with 170,000 passengers stranded," the ministry said in a statement on Sunday.
More than 900 affected flights were to and from the Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, it added.
Several airports in cities including Semarang and Surabaya have been prepared as alternatives for landing, Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said.
- PASSENGERS SCRAMBLING -
The disruption left some passengers scrambling to find alternative flights.
Henny Yensan, 44, who had hoped to go back to her hometown with her mother, said "everybody was disappointed."
"No one flew into a rage because, after all, this is due to natural disaster," the businesswoman who had to reschedule her flight to Tuesday told AFP.
Samuel Guiberteau, a Danone executive on a business trip to Lombok since Friday, said "nothing is certain for the moment", as he searched for alternative flights back to the capital.
"I had found another flight on Citilink, but it was also cancelled," the 47-year-old told AFP by phone, adding that he had no alternative but to stay in Lombok for the time being.
Volcanic ash also reached the city of Bandar Lampung in the southern tip of Sumatra, blanketing parked cars and roadsides.
"I'm worried it could seriously affect the lungs and cause a lung infection," Andre Bayu Saputra, 25, told AFP on Sunday.
Schools across Jakarta will be closed on Monday as classes move online, the city said in a statement, without specifying how long the measure will be in place.
- HAZARD WARNING -
Anak Krakatoa, which means Child of Krakatoa, sits in a strait that separates the islands of Java and Sumatra.
Ships passing through the strait were asked to increase vigilance for possible disruption to navigation safety due to volcanic activities.
Vessels are prohibited from approaching an exclusion zone of three kilometres radius from the volcano, local port authorities said in a statement.
The volcano has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera that formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatoa.
That disaster was one of the deadliest and most destructive in history with an estimated 35,000 people killed.
Geology agency head Lana Saria said "seismic activity indicates the movement or release of volcanic fluids within the volcanic system."
"However, the timing, magnitude, and nature of the next eruption cannot be precisely predicted," Lana added.
Lana warned against approaching Anak Krakatoa, saying materials ejected from the volcano could endanger those within the exclusion zone.
She said the most recent series of eruptions do not have the potential to trigger a tsunami at this time.
A 2018 tsunami triggered by a collapse of parts of Anak Krakatoa killed 429 people and left thousands displaced.
Indonesia, a Southeast Asian archipelago nation, sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where the meeting of continental plates causes high volcanic and seismic activity.--AFP

a12a196ac2ed8627: LONDON: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said his side's performance in Sunday's statement 2-1 victory over Chelsea showed that they can become even better than last season's title-winning model.
Goals by Kai Havertz and captain Martin Odegaard, after Morgan Rogers had scored for Chelsea in the second minute, ensured a third win from three games for Arsenal.
After an easy win against promoted Coventry City and a 1-0 grind at Aston Villa, however, this was the most impressive as Arsenal ripped into the visitors.
"I think it was an exceptional performance. I enjoyed every minute of it from the beginning to the end, and the beginning was tough," Arteta told reporters.
"I enjoyed it because the team reacted in a spectacular way. The conviction, the determination, the quality of which I intend to have them constantly, it was beautiful.
"It's an indication for us of how capable we are to perform at an even higher level than last season, and it depends on how we maintain and sustain that desire."
Arsenal did not beef up their forward options in a relatively quiet transfer window with Brazilian duo Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard departing.
But with Havertz, Odegaard and Bukayo Saka all looking sharp and new signing Christos Tzolis again producing some eye-catching moments out wide, Arsenal looked a real threat.
Norwegian Odegaard, in particular, looks back to his best after last season's injury disruptions.

"Odegaard has a point to prove from last season after missing so much football," Arteta said. "When that happens, Kai the same, Bukayo the same, we miss so many attacking players last season for long, long periods.

"I don't know how many times they've played together those two in the last year or so, but probably not much, and when you start to feel the chemistry they have between them and what they can produce, it's great."

Arsenal and Manchester City are now the only two teams with a 100pct record in the Premier League, while Chelsea's impressive start under new manager Xabi Alonso got a reality check as they dropped their first points under the Spaniard.
His side have now conceded seven goals in three games and while they look a threat in attack, there is clearly work to do at the other end of the pitch.
"We want to start having clean sheets, they will come," Alonso said. "The players are committed to working hard, to knowing that we're on the way to compete in each game.
"Not happy that we couldn't get anything but we need to keep calm and carry on."--REUTERS
89def894a18234a8: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said the country's newest destroyer would be part of a nuclear response system and could deliver "annihilating retaliatory strikes", state media KCNA reported on Monday, although it did not say whether the vessel would carry nuclear weapons.
North Korea has accelerated efforts to modernise its navy as Kim pursues a broader expansion of the country's nuclear-capable forces.
At a commissioning ceremony in the eastern port city of Wonsan on Sunday, Kim said the new ship's deployment to the sea east of the Korean Peninsula sent a clear signal to North Korea's adversaries.
"The time has come for us to exercise our sovereignty at sea and under water," Kim said, according to KCNA.

The 5,000-tonne-class destroyer, the "Kang Kon", is the second warship of its class to enter service, following the commissioning of the "Choe Hyon" destroyer on North Korea's west coast about three months earlier, KCNA cited Kim as saying.

Kim said North Korea's naval nuclear armaments were advancing, and the country would continue to expand what he called its most powerful strategic assets in key waters to protect its maritime sovereignty and regional security.
He added that the Kang Kon would form part of North Korea's state nuclear response system.

KCNA did not specify what weapons systems might be deployed on the Kang Kon, but said is has the same weapons systems as the Choe Hyon. 3347999059a76691: BERLIN: Bavarian minnows Augsburg came from a goal down to a 4-1 win at Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga on Sunday, while a dominant Mainz put five goals past Hamburg.

6092fe1bf048791e: TEHERAN: Iran's top negotiator on Sunday threatened a more forceful response to any further US attacks after Teheran targeted American warships in their latest round of clashes.
The exchanges of fire, which began with US raids last week, come amid a deadlock in the six-month war between the two foes.

CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper had said after the exchange of strikes: "If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost – taking out three of yours."

The administration of US President Donald Trump has tried to downplay the significance of the six-month conflict, which has proven increasingly unpopular at home as midterm elections near.

Trump reiterated that view on Friday, calling the war "small potatoes" for Washington.

Iranian officials have maintained their defiant tone, but US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told ABC's "This Week" programme on Sunday that Iran was "doing everything they can to cling on to something."

A fragile ceasefire between the two sides collapsed in July after attacks on commercial ships in the Hormuz strait, through which one-fifth of world oil supplies previously flowed.

16eeca22d5cbd46b: LONDON: Xabi Alonso urged Chelsea to use their 2-1 defeat at Arsenal on Sunday as a valuable lesson in the race to catch the Premier League champions.

74c1dd3929d2b458: KYIV: US peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff heralded new momentum in peace talks after meeting Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv on Sunday as the Trump administration renewed its push to end Russia's four-and-a-half-year war in Ukraine.

Cautious optimism on the streets of Kyiv
Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Moscow several times in their roles as peace envoys. But Sunday was their first visit to Kyiv in their capacity as US negotiators.

08d33e245aec13d8: NEW YORK: Aryna Sabalenka kept her US Open three-peat bid alive Sunday, charging into the US Open quarter-finals with a confidence-boosting victory over tricky American Taylor Townsend.

e633af80e01169ca: MIAMI: At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after it landed Sunday at Miami International Airport, crashed into vehicles and caught fire, officials said.

5b66995855f063c0: LONDON: Arsenal delivered an emphatic response to Chelsea's emergence as potential Premier League title contenders with a 2-1 win that ended their rivals' unbeaten start on Sunday.

a5121b854fb303ae: TAIZ: The toll from days of fighting between government forces and Iran-backed Houthi rebels in southwest Yemen climbed past 300 on Sunday, as hundreds of families fled their homes to escape the violence.

Two military officials with the Saudi-backed government forces told AFP that 84 of their troops were killed between midday Saturday and early Sunday morning, mostly in missile attacks. Four Houthi military sources said 57 rebel fighters were killed in the same period.

With Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial ships, the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint has gained importance as a transit route, connecting Asia to Europe via the Suez Canal.
In July, a fragile truce between the Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed government fell apart after the rebels welcomed an Iranian plane to the capital Sanaa, setting off a spate of attacks.
The Houthis have also announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and have begun targeting its ships and territory.

Japan plans to probe into popular animal cafes, where visitors can interact with anything from cats to capybaras, following concerns about hygiene and the creatures' welfare.
Japan has hundreds of these cafes where campaigners say animals are sometimes kept in cramped spaces and that their popularity encourages the capture and illegal trade of rare wildlife.
A fact-finding survey will begin as early as next month, starting with obtaining basic facts such as the number of establishments and what animals they keep, an Environment Ministry official said.
The ministry will examine whether they comply with laws, including whether animals have enough space and how often cleaning takes place, said the official.
"We may then do on-site inspections if we find facilities that appear to be breaching rules stipulated by the animal welfare law," he said.
The decision to launch the survey followed recommendations by members of an expert panel about animal welfare.
Animal welfare groups have long been alarmed by the cafes, where visitors can pet and play with a dizzying array of animals, including micro-pigs, hedgehogs, owls and snakes.

OSLO: The uncrewed Spectrum rocket was the first commercial flight to reach orbit from continental Europe, where several nations have said they want a share of a growing market for space missions.

Blasting off from Norway's Arctic Andoeya Spaceport, Spectrum — designed for small and medium-sized payloads — carried five small satellites, as well as an in-flight technological experiment, according to Isar.

It was Isar's second launch, coming 18 months after the company's first rocket plunged into the sea and exploded in a fiery spectacle shortly after takeoff from the same site. No one was injured at the time.
Saturday's launch was intended as "both the vehicle's qualification mission and its first flight carrying payload", the Bavarian company has said.

Global players in the satellite launch market include Elon Musk's SpaceX, which launches from the US, and French ArianeGroup, a joint venture between Airbus and Safran that uses a spaceport in South America's French Guiana.
Sweden, with its Esrange launch site and Britain, with its SaxaVord Spaceport in the Scottish Shetland Islands, are the nearest rivals to the Norwegian site.
Isar last week said it had secured about 200 million euros from the European Space Agency to help fund development of new rockets and expand its testing and launch infrastructure.
The German company is also developing a second launch site in Canada.

KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission (SC) and Bursa Malaysia Bhd have launched the inaugural InvestSmart x Bursa Marketplace Fair 2026 to promote investor education and protect investors against scams.
The two-day event brings together the SC and Bursa Malaysia's flagship investor engagement platforms for the first time.
It was officiated by Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.
The collaboration highlights the importance of investor education and financial literacy as more Malaysians explore a wider range of investment products, digital platforms and information sources.
The SC said the collaboration reflects a shared commitment by both organisations to strengthen investor education.
By bringing together the two flagship investor engagement platforms, both organisations aim to reach more people and promote informed investing and investor protection.
The event combines investor education, market insights and practical guidance to help participants evaluate investment opportunities, understand risks and spot potential scams.
SC chairman Datuk Mohammad Faiz Azmi said broader participation in the capital market remains essential to support a financially resilient and inclusive society.
"For many Malaysians, concerns about fraud and limited access to reliable investment information remain barriers to investing.

"This collaboration aims to improve access to trusted financial information and digital investment tools, empowering more Malaysians to invest with confidence and take greater charge of their long-term financial wellbeing."

Faiz said the SC remains committed to strengthening investor education and financial literacy through strategic partnerships, including with the National Scam Response Centre and the Financial Education Network.

From January to July 2026, the SC received 1,272 enquiries, or 70.6 per cent of cases, from people seeking to verify investment opportunities before investing, compared with 530 complaints, or 29.4 per cent, from scam victims.
The higher proportion of enquiries points to greater awareness of the need to conduct due diligence before investing.

Bursa Malaysia chief executive officer Datuk Fad'l Mohamed said the local capital market offers a wide range of opportunities, while growing participation, particularly among younger investors, reflects greater interest in building financial resilience.

"By bringing market experts, listed companies and financial institutions under one roof, we hope to make it easier for more Malaysians to explore investment opportunities, build their knowledge and take the next step from saving to investing.
"This supports our broader goal of fostering a vibrant and inclusive capital market that enables more Malaysians to participate in and benefit from the nation's economic growth."

Retail participation in the capital market continues to grow, with more than 342,000 new Central Depository System (CDS) accounts opened in the first six months of 2026, up about 24 per cent from the same period last year.
Around 60 per cent of the new accounts were opened by investors aged 35 and under, showing growing participation among younger Malaysians.
Retail investors also accounted for between 27 per cent and 33 per cent of total trading activity over the past three years.

The fair brings together up to 40 exhibitors, giving visitors access to market experts, financial intermediaries, regulators, publicly listed companies, crowdfunding platforms and other industry practitioners.

4c198d70a37efbed: TEHRAN: Iranian authorities on Sunday announced they were raising the price of petrol for heavier consumers, as the United States steps up sanctions seeking to isolate the country's economy.

Iran's quota system prices petrol in three tiers - 1,500 tomans per litre for a consumer's first 60 litres in a given month, 3,000 tomans per litre for their next 50, and 5,000 tomans per litre after that. The toman is an informal unit equivalent to 10 Iranian rials.

"Different numbers were mentioned in expert meetings, but because the president had promised the people, the rate of 10,000 tomans was set," she added.
She later clarified that the price of the first and second tiers would not be changed.
Iran, a major oil producer with some of the world's cheapest fuel, has for years heavily subsidised petrol, making any changes to pricing politically sensitive.

4abade6444b79d5a: KATHMANDU: The UN chief in Nepal issued an emotional plea for aid on Sunday, saying survivors of the catastrophic flooding had seen their lives transformed in just "one to two minutes".

After visiting battered mountain communities, UN Resident Coordinator Lila Pieters Yahia told AFP that people were struggling to comprehend how suddenly their Himalayan homes had become an expanse of ruin and destruction.
"You lose your home, you lose your livelihood, you lose your loved one and you lose the breadwinner of your family," Pieters Yahia said in Kathmandu.
"And you know, this happened in one to two minutes," Pieters Yahia.
The devastating Aug 26 flood that crashed through the China-Nepal border killed at least 1,384 people and left more than 5,500 missing across both countries.
More than 800 foreigners from at least 34 countries are among those missing in both Nepal and Tibet in China. They include both tourists and pilgrims.
Many communities near the epicentre of the disaster remain cut off, with the UN working alongside Nepal's government to get emergency supplies into devastated areas.
The UN has launched a US$50 million appeal to help more than 84,000 people affected by the disaster.
"Those people are cut off from the rest of the world because the road is gone," Pieters Yahia said.
"You try to find a solution to expedite access, and you find another bottleneck. We're looking into all means, but we need to to improve access."
'Risk of cholera'
Floods tore through mountain districts, destroying roads, bridges and hydropower dams.
The destruction means journeys that once took a couple of hours have now become day-long ordeals.
"The Himalayas are beautiful, they are amazing, they're spiritual," said Pieters Yahia.
"But also they are very, very difficult terrains... And we have the landslides -- and, plus we're still in the monsoon season."
She warned that beyond immediate shelter and food needs, authorities would have to guard against disease outbreaks and work to protect vulnerable women and girls.
Citing government data, she said 5,000 cattle had died in the flooding.
"This is a big issue because this could lead to communicable diseases... We may have risk of cholera, so this is why immediately we have to invest in sanitation and hygiene."
Pieters Yahia called for greater international support for Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people with limited resources.
"My plea to the international community is: this is the time to help Nepal. It's not tomorrow and it's not yesterday," she said.
"We can't leave them there. We can't leave them alone," she added.

72002d180906febb: KANAZAWA, Sept 6 — In the historic Japanese city of Kanazawa, craftsmen painstakingly shape and slice blocks of ice destined to chill negronis in some of the world’s trendiest bars.
The men work for Kuramoto Ice, a century-old company in Ishikawa on the Sea of Japan coast and one of dozens of Japanese firms producing ultra-clear, premium ice.
This luxury product, believed by those in the industry to melt more slowly than regular blocks, is a staple of Japan’s cocktail culture.
But its popularity is also spilling over to bars abroad, from the United States to Australia, who pay as much as 200 yen (US$1.25) per cube.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Ice spheres sit in a basket after being cut at the Kuramoto Ice factory. — AFP pic
Kuramoto Ice is of the country’s few international exporters, and has seen total sales more than double since exports began in 2019.
“We take our time and freeze water slowly, keeping it in motion... That’s how we end up with good ice,” Kazuhiko Kuramoto, the firm’s fifth-generation head, told AFP at their Kanazawa factory.
“My heart leaps with joy when I see ice that looks like a jewel,” said the 41-year-old, as he poured cold hojicha tea into a glass filled with a large, clear sphere.

Using a technique that originally came from the United States, specialist Japanese ice makers freeze water over a period of 48 to 72 hours, far longer than the few hours typically required for homemade ice or the 30 minutes it takes industrial ice machines.

As freezing begins and the ice forms from outside in, various impurities in the water get pushed towards the centre. But the Japanese method involves removing that tainted water and replacing it with a fresh batch. Constant stirring helps remove air bubbles, resulting in completely transparent ice, known as “junpyo” in Japanese.
Although there is little scientific evidence, it’s said the technique also results in a colder, denser product that will cool rather than dilute a cocktail.
Native — a trendy bar in Singapore that made this year’s Asia’s 50 Best Bars list — imports around 900 kilograms of ice from Kuramoto each year.
“Local ice is more economical, but Kuramoto Ice is clearer, denser and melts more slowly,” co-owner Yong Wei told AFP.
‘Lingering aftertaste’

In Kanazawa, workers dressed in full-body overalls haul large blocks of ice across the factory floor, before starting on the delicate work of carving perfect spheres, cubes and rectangular blocks with cut corners.
Once packaged, the finished products — which can be made to precisely fit any glass — are stored in a room at minus 10 degrees before shipment.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
This picture taken on June 15, 2026 shows the Kuramoto Ice factory in Kanazawa. — AFP pic

Boss Kuramoto is not blind to the environmental cost of transporting cubes of ice thousands of kilometres across the world, but insisted that small goods like his have a relatively low environmental impact.

He said he had dreamed of reaching American bars since visiting Las Vegas more than a decade ago and realising low-quality ice that melts easily and waters down the flavour was being used in expensive cocktails.
The time-consuming ice-making technique often used in Japan, which tends to produce a higher quality product, had largely been phased out in the US.
At a Hilton Hotel bar near Tokyo, bartender Shingo Miyachi prepares a negroni with one of Kuramoto Ice’s big, clear cubes.
The ice fits perfectly in the glass, and its clarity makes it almost invisible.
“Ice really has a huge impact on the taste of a cocktail,” Miyachi told AFP.
If it melts, “it especially affects the lingering aftertaste once you’ve taken a sip.”
Ice handling is considered an essential skill for Japanese bartenders, who often begin their training by learning to break it with precision.

“When you look at the ice and see the level of attention to detail, you can pretty much tell how seriously the bartender takes the flavour of the cocktail and how much care they’ve put into it,” he explained.
“A cocktail only really comes into being when the glass, the ice, and the liquid become one as a single unified whole.” — AFP

Agence France-Presse photographer Luis Tato on Saturday won the top prize at the prestigious Visa Pour l’Image photojournalism festival in Perpignan, France. — AFP pic

In September 2025, student-led protests erupted across Madagascar over failing public services, corruption, and economic hardship. When President Andry Rajoelina dissolved his government but refused to resign, demonstrations intensified.

“I think this global movement of young people who are trying to redefine democracy and transform their societies is a very interesting dynamic, which fascinates me both as a photographer and as someone who seeks to understand the world we live in,” said Tato.

c22a34e50d42498f: SEPTEMBER 6 — The departure board says “DELAYED”. Then “CANCELLED”. Around you, children are sleeping on luggage, phones are being charged wherever a socket can be found, and somewhere beyond the airport, an Indonesian volcano is quietly changing thousands of travel plans.
If you are one of those waiting tonight, let me tell you a story.
It is a story about a very large aeroplane, a very powerful volcano and a night when nature reminded human beings that sometimes the safest journey is the one we postpone.

On June 24, 1982, British Airways Flight BA009 was flying from Kuala Lumpur towards Perth. The aircraft was a Boeing 747-200 named City of Edinburgh, cruising at around 37,000 feet above Indonesia when it entered something the crew could not see: volcanic ash from Mount Galunggung in West Java.
And here is something remarkable for Malaysian travellers sitting in an airport tonight: BA009 began its journey in Kuala Lumpur.
The passengers had expected an ordinary flight to Perth. Instead, somewhere above Indonesia, their journey became anything but ordinary.
Passengers first noticed what appeared to be smoke inside the cabin. Then came strange flashes outside the windows. The aircraft began to shake.
One engine failed.
Then another.
Then another.
Then the fourth.
All four engines were silent.

For the aviation enthusiasts among you, here is a detail worth remembering. That mighty 747 was powered by four Rolls-Royce RB211 engines — four enormous turbofans built to carry a Jumbo across oceans.
That night, all four fell silent.

Not because the aircraft was defective. Not because the pilots had made a reckless decision. A volcano had simply placed an invisible hazard directly into their flight path. Volcanic ash entered the engines, causing them to surge and eventually flame out.
For a moment, the mighty Jumbo was no longer a machine of power. It was simply a glider in the dark.

The pilots began descending. Passengers put on their oxygen masks. The cabin grew quiet. Some prayed. Some held hands. Some thought about their families. Some simply sat there, trying to understand what was happening.
And yet, remarkably, there was no mass panic.
People helped one another. Cabin crew reassured passengers. Travellers looked after children and elderly passengers. Some prayed; others simply tried to remain calm.
And the crew kept doing their job.

As the aircraft descended below the ash, the engines eventually began to come back to life. One, then another, then another. The great Rolls-Royce engines that had fallen silent began to breathe again.
The aircraft eventually landed safely in Jakarta.
Everyone survived.

Decades later, researchers interviewed some of those passengers and crew. They remembered the fear, but they also remembered kindness, responsibility, the calmness of the crew and the simple human instinct to care for one another when faced with uncertainty.
Perhaps that is the part of BA009 we should remember tonight.
If you are sitting in an Indonesian airport, waiting for a cancelled flight, you are not failing to get home.
You are waiting for the right moment to get home. There is a difference.

And if you are Malaysian, perhaps this story belongs to you a little more than you realise. Forty-four years ago, other Malaysians and travellers began their journey from Kuala Lumpur expecting to arrive in Perth. Instead, they found themselves confronting an Indonesian volcano thousands of feet above the ground.
They had a destination too.
They had somewhere they wanted to be.
And they, too, had to wait for the sky to allow them through.
So take a breath.
If your family is waiting anxiously for your message, call them. Tell them you are safe. Tell them the flight can wait. Tell them you will come home when the sky is ready.

The volcano has spoken, not with words but with ash. It has travelled through the sky and reminded us that nature does not consult our itineraries. Sometimes the departure board must surrender to something much older and more powerful than our schedules.
Tonight, perhaps, the mountain is simply asking us to wait.
Safety does not always look like movement.
Sometimes, safety looks like staying exactly where you are.

So call your mother. Call your father. Call the person waiting for you. Tell them you are all right. Hug the child beside you. Hold the hand of the person travelling with you. Share your charger with someone whose phone is dying. Let the tired child sleep.
And if you are alone, look around. You are surrounded by thousands of other people who, just like you, were supposed to be somewhere else tonight.
You are not alone in waiting.
Please remember this: a cancelled flight is an inconvenience. A flight sent into a dangerous ash cloud can become a tragedy.
The people keeping you on the ground tonight are not keeping you from your destination.
They are protecting your journey.

Forty-four years ago, a mighty Boeing 747 nearly bowed to the wrath of an Indonesian volcano. Tonight, we have something BA009's passengers did not have. We know. We can see the ash. We can track the volcano. We can close the runway.
We can wait.
And sometimes, safety is nothing more complicated than having the courage to say:
Not tonight.
So rest, traveller. Let the volcano speak. Let the ash settle. Let the engines wait.
Your destination will still be there tomorrow.
And to every Indonesian traveller waiting to continue your journey, and every Malaysian traveller longing for home:
Welcome home soon.
Not tonight, perhaps.
But soon.
And somewhere, someone who loves you is waiting to hear three simple words:
“I'm okay. I'm safe.”
Tonight, that is enough.
* Dr Marziah Zahar is a senior lecturer in Safety, Health and Environmental at the School of Business Management, Universiti Utara Malaysia.

4c40c127c96cbeb2: GAZA CITY, Sept 6 — Palestinians held a funeral procession on Sunday for 100 people whose remains were recovered from under the rubble of destroyed homes in Gaza City’s Zeitoun neighbourhood following Israel’s genocidal war on the enclave, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.

Thousands of Palestinians, including relatives of the victims as well as community and political figures, attended the procession, with the remains laid out in an area near the ruins of the destroyed homes and draped in Palestinian flags.
The funeral includes memorial addresses by Gaza’s Civil Defence, whose teams carried out the recovery operations, as well as representatives of the victims’ families and community figures.
The remains are expected to be buried at Al-Ahli cemetery in the Zeitoun neighbourhood after funeral prayers.

Civil Defence teams recovered them in recent days as part of the second phase of a project launched on July 19 to retrieve the remains of Palestinians still buried beneath the rubble of buildings destroyed during the Israeli war.

The victims belonged to the Rahim, Balawi, Malaka, Qanbour and Salmi families and were killed when Israeli forces struck several residential homes around two and a half years ago, according to local authorities.

Recovery operations are being carried out with limited resources, including only a small number of excavators and deteriorating equipment, amid Israeli restrictions on the entry of heavy machinery and equipment needed to search the rubble.
Sunday’s ceremony is among the largest funerals in Palestinian history in terms of the number of bodies and remains being buried, according to an Anadolu tally.
A similar funeral was held in early August for 112 Palestinians recovered from the rubble of homes in Gaza City’s Sabra neighbourhood.

The second phase of the recovery project involves 800 hours of work at 147 destroyed homes across Gaza City and the northern and central parts of the enclave, where 1,072 remains are believed to still be buried.

The first phase began in late November 2025 and involved 500 hours of work. Civil Defence teams recovered around 333 remains out of an estimated 559 missing beneath the rubble of 54 homes and buildings.

Under the first phase of the Gaza ceasefire agreement, in effect since Oct 10, 2025, Israel was expected to allow the entry of heavy machinery and equipment needed for recovery operations, according to Palestinian authorities in the enclave.

The ceasefire followed nearly two years of Israeli attacks on Gaza, which killed more than 73,000 Palestinians and injured over 174,000, while destroying or damaging much of the enclave’s civilian infrastructure. — Bernama-Anadolu

ced28f0ed87d870e: SEPTEMBER 7 — Malaysia should not congratulate itself too quickly. But neither should it ignore something that has become increasingly apparent during the prolonged global energy crisis: the country has so far handled the fuel shock relatively well.
The contrast with parts of Asean is becoming increasingly significant.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s economic adviser, Nurhisham Hussein, said Malaysia’s fuel supply remains stable despite tightening global supplies. Petronas is confident that sufficient supplies can be secured through the end of the year.
More importantly, Malaysia has avoided the kind of severe physical shortages that an international energy crisis could easily have produced.
That is no small achievement.

But Nurhisham’s second observation deserves even greater attention. Oil prices may remain elevated for another two to three years. Countries that have drawn down their reserves are unlikely to rebuild them aggressively until prices return to something closer to US$80 a barrel.
In other words, this is no longer merely an energy-price spike.
It could become a prolonged period of expensive energy.

Malaysia enters this difficult environment with several advantages. It is a significant oil and gas producer, a net exporter of liquefied natural gas, possesses substantial domestic energy infrastructure and, above all, has Petronas.
The government has also chosen not to expose households completely to international price fluctuations.

The basic monthly eligibility for subsidised RON95 has been restored to 300 litres, with the subsidised price remaining RM1.99 per litre. Malaysia’s overall inflation, meanwhile, remains around two per cent.
This is an important economic buffer.
Petrol prices are not simply another item in the consumer price index.
Energy runs through almost everything: transportation, logistics, food distribution, manufacturing, aviation, fisheries and eventually the price of goods on supermarket shelves.
A government that prevents an international oil shock from immediately becoming a domestic cost-of-living shock therefore buys valuable economic and political breathing space.
Much of Asean is not quite so fortunate.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Motorists queue to refuel at a petrol station in Hanoi on March 10, 2026. — AFP pic
The Philippines is particularly vulnerable because of its dependence on imported energy, relatively modest buffers and rapid transmission of international energy prices into domestic costs.

Thailand is similarly exposed through its large oil and gas trade deficit. Indonesia has greater domestic energy resources but must contend with the enormous fiscal cost of shielding its population from international prices.
This is the fundamental Asean dilemma.

Governments can allow international oil prices to pass through to consumers and risk inflation, declining purchasing power and political dissatisfaction. Or they can subsidise energy heavily and transfer the shock onto government budgets.
Neither option is painless.
Indeed, fossil-fuel support across South-east Asia was estimated at US$353.1 billion in 2024 when explicit and implicit subsidies are included.
Elevated energy prices therefore represent not merely an energy-security problem but an increasingly serious fiscal challenge.
Malaysia’s relative success should consequently be understood as strategic management rather than immunity.
Kuala Lumpur still has to pay for subsidies. Businesses remain vulnerable to higher diesel, electricity, transportation and input costs.
An extended period of expensive crude could eventually work its way through supply chains regardless of government intervention.
Nor can Malaysia ignore what happens to its neighbours.

Asean is an interconnected production platform. If transportation costs rise sharply in Thailand, manufacturing costs increase in Vietnam, inflation accelerates in the Philippines or Indonesia is forced to divert billions more into energy subsidies, Malaysia will eventually feel the consequences through trade, investment and regional demand.
Energy security must therefore become an Asean issue rather than merely ten separate national problems.
The Asean Power Grid becomes even more important in this environment.
So does diversification towards renewable energy, stronger regional electricity interconnection, electric vehicles, improved public transportation and greater energy efficiency.
Interestingly, China’s rapid adoption of electric vehicles is already helping moderate global petroleum demand, according to Nurhisham.
There is a lesson here for Asean.
Energy transition should no longer be viewed exclusively through the prism of climate change. It is increasingly about strategic autonomy.

Every additional unit of electricity generated domestically from solar, hydroelectricity or other renewable sources potentially reduces exposure to distant conflicts and vulnerable maritime chokepoints.

The West Asian crisis has demonstrated brutally how geopolitical instability thousands of kilometres away can reach directly into the household budgets of South-east Asians. More than 80 per cent of the crude oil and LNG passing through the Strait of Hormuz is normally destined for Asia.
Malaysia has managed this difficult period better than might have been expected.

Stable supplies, targeted fuel support, Petronas’ international reach and relatively contained inflation have provided the country with buffers that several Asean neighbours do not possess to the same degree.
But if Nurhisham is correct that elevated oil prices could persist for another two or three years, Malaysia cannot merely congratulate itself for surviving the first stage of the crisis.
It should use the breathing space to prepare for the next one.
And Malaysia should help Asean do the same.
Energy resilience cannot stop at Malaysia’s borders. In an integrated Asean economy, Malaysia cannot remain permanently fortunate if its neighbours are increasingly unfortunate.
* Phar Kim Beng, PhD is the Professor of Asean Studies at International Islamic University of Malaysia and Director of Institute of International and Asean Studies (IINTAS).
** This is the personal opinion of the writers or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

40dc1ce96b111174: The prospect of a negative leap second – combined with decades of irritation over leap seconds generally – looks set to inspire a bit of global procrastination among international timekeepers. Next month, the General Conference on Weights and Measures is set to vote on effectively calling time on leap seconds. A draft resolution [PDF] would make Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) continuous from May 20, 2027, and allow the difference between UTC and UT1, a measure of time based on Earth's rotation, to reach as much as one hour. Leap seconds keep UTC, which is based on atomic clocks, within 0.9 seconds of time determined by the slightly wobbly rotation of our home planet. Since the system was introduced in 1972, 27 leap seconds have been added to UTC. The urgency comes partly from a slight increase in Earth's rotational speed in recent years, raising the possibility of an adjustment never attempted before: a negative leap second. Experts convened by international timekeeping bodies estimated a 30 percent probability that one would be needed by 2035. Many computer systems were designed on the assumption that a leap second would always be added rather than removed, explained Setnam Shemar, principal scientist at the UK's National Physical Laboratory (NPL). "Most digital architectures and network time servers are hardcoded under the assumption that leap seconds are strictly additive. Losing a second could trigger severe disruption across critical national infrastructure, including telecommunications, electricity grids, and satellite navigation systems," he said. The risks posed by a negative leap second – and leap seconds generally – are behind the proposal to let UTC diverge from rotational time by as much as an hour, which is due to be put to a vote in October. Shemar said the proposal would remove the need for further leap-second adjustments for many years. "This would remove the risks entirely for a very long time. Next month's resolution is likely to pass since it will be based on the outcome of a majority vote of the national delegates from many different countries, and most of them have been keen to end leap seconds for several years due to the risks posed to national infrastructure." UTC would be unlikely to diverge from rotational time by a full hour for at least a thousand years, Shemar said. If humankind lasts that long, it might be the least of our worries. ®

bfdce3ac86d9c7bc: Kehebatan Tun M dalam politik memang tidak ada siapa yang boleh tandingi. Sama ada beliau berkuasa atau tidak, gelagat dan kata dua beliau akan sering menjadi buah mulut rakyat sekalian. Itu hebatnya Mahathir.

Beliau tidak perlu guna ayat al-Quran langsung dan tidak perlu ceramah berjela-jela dalam Facebook, cuma datang, duduk atas kerusi roda dan senyum sambil melambai. Itu pun sudah cukup untuk memulakan ribut taufan bersama halilintar.

Kenapa Tun M tak dijemput secara rasmi, 'sound' beberapa influencer yang becok berceloteh. Inikan suatu ketidakadilan kepada seorang tokoh negara? Sebenarnya saya pun agak setuju dengan teguran ini tetapi ada lima perkara yang perlu kita semua renungi dahulu.

Perkara pertama adalah apa yang disebut oleh Rafizi dalam podcastnya bila ditanya tentang isu ini. Saya berterima kasih dengan Rafizi yang memberi maklumat yang kita semua pun tak tahu. Kata Rafizi, Tun M sendiri yang mengubah protokol menjemput bekas perdana menteri untuk majlis penting seperti merdeka pada 2018.

Rafizi memberi alasan takkanlah Tun M nak duduk sebelah seorang penjenayah dan seteru beliau. Tetapi ada influencer yang tegur, Najib belum penjenayah lagi sebab baru buka kes. So, what’s the problem? Yang penting, seperti biasa, Tun memang bijak baling batu dan sembunyi tangan sambil senyum dan melambai.

Perkara kedua, kalaulah kita ada protokol untuk menjemput bekas perdana menteri atau kita ikut adab Melayu lah untuk jemput orang besar-besar, I must assume yang protokol tu dibuat dengan anggapan bahawa bekas perdana menteri tidak lagi berpolitik.

Dalam kes Tun M, beliau masih giat berpolitik dan rasanya sanggup memegang tampuk kerajaan sebagai PM untuk kali ketiga! Jadi, kalau begini rupanya, patutkah PM sedia ada menjemput seterunya dalam politik ke pentas Merdeka?

Perkara ketiga pula adalah Tun M telah membuat naratif bahawa Melayu akan hilang kuasa kalau tidak duduk di bawah satu payung besar. Sudah tentulah, payung tu dia yang punya. Jadi kalau semua Melayu duduk di situ kita boleh teka tiga kali siapa akan jadi PM.

Namun demikian, apa yang saya gusarkan adalah dengan membina naratif ini maka ia membuat suatu permusuhan dengan rakyat lain bukan Melayu termasuk Bumiputra semua. Patutkah seorang bekas PM yang menerajui negara dua kali dan masih membina naratif permusuhan antara Melayu dan bukan Melayu dijemput ke pentas duduk bersama parti PH yang tidak pernah menggunakan ras atau isu perkauman?
Saya pun tidak tergamak untuk duduk sebelah orang sebegini, tidak kisah lah dia PM berapa kali pun. Orang yang membuat kita bermusuh-musuh, bagi saya batang tubuh itu lah musuh terbesar negara kita.

Nasib baik Tun M tidak jadi seperti seorang guru agama yang nak buat kita bermusuh antara orang Islam dan bukan Islam, yang itu lagi ‘haru’ kata orang utara. Saya rasa Tun M baik sikit daripada tok guru agama yang pandai tafsir Quran ikut suka dia.

Perkara keempat adalah Tun M telah pernah membuat naratif Malaysia ini bukan negara multicultural sebab tidak ada disebutkan dalam konsep Malaysia secara undang-undang. Sekali lagi beliau memainkan isu ‘pendatang’ dan memainkan lagu lama bahawa pendatang akan take over everything kalau Melayu tak sedar dan tak bersatu. Same old song but very efective still.

Maklumlah orang Melayu ramai tidak belajar falsafah dan sejarah peradaban dunia. Kebanyakan Melayu belajar kejuruteraan, seni bina, perubatan, undang-undang dan bila pencen baru mengadap kuliah agama.

Mahathir adalah seorang pembaca tegar dan dia faham selok belok sejarah Malaysia dan dunia. Sejarah subjek kegemarannya, saya baca dalam buku beliau A Doctor in the House. Saya memang baca banyak buku Tun M, saya rasa empat buah kesemuanya. Jadi, kita kena tanya diri kita sebagai rakyat, do we want someone yang tidak admit kita negara multicultural?

Perkara kelima, memanglah dari satu sudut, kita patut jemput orang tua itu. Memang kita patut honor seorang pemimpin seperti Tun M. Tetapi jika batang tubuh itu sendiri bergerak untuk mengkucar-kacirkan kita semua, what should we do?

Dalam bab itu, Tun M memainkan peranan kita sebagai a united rakyat to save our country. Tetapi apabila beliau memainkan sentimen perkauman untuk menjatuhkan kerajaan perpaduan, that is an entirely different matter.

Maka itu, kita kena renung sendiri sama ada kita nak bagi hormat atau tidak kepada orang seperti Tun M. Saya sendiri amat menghormati beliau dalam banyak perkara seperti ketegasan beliau tentang ekstremis agama, tentang menimba ilmu dan memahirkan diri dalam sains, teknologi dan Bahasa Inggeris.

Itu jalur pemisah antara Merdeka sebagai rakyat dengan mereka yang nak menjatuhkan idea negara-bangsa kita.

a4b3f6287a5a5dbc: Saya mengikuti muktamar PAS yang sedang berlangsung di Pengkalan Chepa, Kelantan dari jauh. Ramai yang hadir dan ramai juga wakil yang berpidato dan dari situ, banyak persoalan yang timbul di benak saya.
Saya tidak banyak mendengar ucapan khusus tentang masalah negeri atau negara, apalagi tentang hal-hal yang berkait dengan ekonomi rakyat atau ekonomi negara.

Ataupun tentang hutang negara yang begitu tinggi, masalah kewangan defisit, perbelanjaan kerajaan berlebihan, Belanjawan 2027, pembahagian hasil dan pendapatan, serta bagaimana semua ini akan diuruskan sekiranya PAS mengambil alih tampuk pemerintahan negara.

Persoalan saya di sini, bukan sekadar sama ada PAS mampu memenangi pilihan raya akan datang dan membentuk kerajaan. Mereka yang hadir nampaknya percaya dan agak yakin. Sebagai contoh, 'Time for PAS to lead with its own PM candidate, says youth leader', satu impian besar yang perlu sedikit kajian dan penjelasan.
Persoalan yang lebih besar ialah: adakah PAS benar-benar mempunyai keupayaan, kepakaran dan kerangka dasar yang jelas untuk mentadbir sebuah negara majmuk?

Berapa ramai pakar ekonomi, tokoh fiskal atau kewangan, perdagangan, pendidikan, industri, pengangkutan dan pembangunan dalam PAS? Apakah mereka sekadar bergantung harap kepada rakan politiknya semata-mata?

Siapa dalam kalangan mereka yang berkaliber untuk membentuk dasar baharu? Siapakah antara yang hadir, mampu melakukan perubahan pengurusan negara supaya Malaysia bukan sekadar ditadbir, tetapi benar-benar dimajukan ke tahap yang lebih baik dan lebih tinggi?
Memerintah Malaysia bukan hanya sekadar menjadi perdana menteri, menteri atau timbalan menteri.

Ia memerlukan satu pasukan yang mempunyai kepakaran, pengalaman dan keberanian untuk membuat keputusan yang sukar, khususnya apabila berhadapan dengan masalah fiskal, hutang negara, subsidi, pelaburan, perdagangan, pendidikan, hubungan antarabangsa dan hubungan antara kerajaan persekutuan dengan Sabah dan Sarawak.
Rakyat perlu tahu apakah sebenarnya visi dan misi PAS untuk Malaysia.
Dasar fiskal
Pada pandangan saya, antara perkara paling penting yang akan menentukan kejayaan atau kegagalan mana-mana kerajaan baharu ialah dasar fiskal mereka.

Dasar fiskal ini menentukan bagaimana kerajaan memperolehi hasil, siapa yang membayar cukai, bagaimana wang dibelanjakan, siapa yang menerima bantuan dan bagaimana defisit serta hutang negara dikawal, menjadi seimbang atau ada lebihan (surplus). Di sinilah PAS perlu memberikan perhatian utama dengan pandangan yang pandai, padat dan serius.

Cadangan “Please change the movie on tax” oleh Geoffrey Williams, misalnya, merupakan satu cadangan dasar fiskal yang menarik dan wajar diberi perhatian. Tiada seorang pun yang hadir di muktamar PAS menyentuh tentang hal yang penting seperti ini.
Cadangan menggunakan electronic payment tax (EPT) sebagai mekanisme percukaian baharu, jika dilaksanakan dengan reka bentuk yang betul, berpotensi mengubah cara kerajaan mengutip hasil.

Sekiranya PAS benar-benar mahu memimpin Putrajaya, saya berpendapat mereka perlu mendengar pandangan pakar seperti beliau dan pakar-pakar dari kaum lain yang mempunyai kepakaran dalam percukaian dan kewangan awam. Persoalannya ialah: apakah model percukaian alternatif yang PAS mahu dan akan diperkenalkan?

Adakah PAS akan terus bergantung kepada sistem cukai sedia ada (SST dan GST) atau mempunyai keberanian untuk memperkenalkan pendekatan baharu yang lebih luas asasnya, lebih cekap kutipannya dan lebih adil kepada rakyat?

Jika EPT mampu direka dengan baik sehingga kutipan hasil kerajaan menjadi lebih cekap tanpa terlalu membebankan golongan berpendapatan rendah, ia boleh menjadi sebahagian daripada reset fiskal negara. Tetapi ini memerlukan kajian, kepakaran dan perancangan yang sangat teliti.

Kerajaan tetap memerlukan hasil yang mencukupi untuk membiayai kos pengurusan, belanjawan untuk pendidikan, kesihatan, keselamatan, pengangkutan awam, infrastruktur dan pembangunan negara. Justeru, PAS perlu menjelaskan bukan sahaja berapa banyak cukai yang mahu dikutip, tetapi daripada siapa, dengan cara bagaimana dan untuk membiayai apa.
Defisit, hutang dan ketirisan

Terkait dengan dasar fiskal ialah belanjawan defisit Malaysia setiap tahun yang telah melangkau lebih dua puluh lapan tahun, sejak 1998. Belanjawan defisit ini membuatkan hutang kerajaan terus meningkat, yang kini sudah melebihi RM1.38 trilion atau sejumlah 64% daripada kadar Keluaran Dalam Negara Kasar. Dalam keadaan sebegini, setiap ringgit wang negara dan wang rakyat sepatutnya diurus dengan penuh amanah, telus dan berdisiplin. Ini yang harus disahut oleh PAS.

Masalahnya bukan sekadar kerajaan berbelanja terlalu banyak. Persoalan yang lebih besar ialah ke mana wang itu dibelanjakan, berapa banyak yang benar-benar sampai kepada rakyat dan berapa banyak yang hilang akibat ketirisan, pembaziran, penyelewengan, rasuah dan salah guna kuasa.

Sebab itu, jika PAS benar-benar serius untuk mengambil alih Putrajaya, rakyat berhak menuntut satu kenyataan dan pendirian yang jelas, tegas dan tidak berkompromi mengenai rasuah dan salah guna kuasa, khususnya apabila ia melibatkan wang negara dan wang simpanan rakyat.

Tanpa kenyataan yang kukuh dan meyakinkan mengenai perkara ini, pendirian PAS boleh ditafsirkan sebagai tidak serius, lemah dan akhirnya memudaratkan negara. Apalagi di muktamar kali ini, PAS mengundang parti-parti politik yang terjebak dengan gejala rasuah dan salahguna kuasa tersebut.
Ini bukan lagi soal politik kepartian atau rakan kongsi politik. Ini soal wang negara dan wang rakyat, yang memerlukan kerangka polisi yang wajar dan kuat.

Apabila negara mempunyai hutang yang begitu besar dan terus berbelanja dalam keadaan belanjawan defisit, kerajaan tidak boleh pada masa yang sama membiarkan ruang untuk ketirisan, pembaziran dan penyelewengan terus terbuka dan berlaku.

Setiap ketirisan akhirnya perlu dibayar oleh rakyat -- sama ada melalui cukai yang lebih tinggi, pengurangan subsidi, pengurangan perkhidmatan awam, pinjaman baharu atau hutang yang akan ditanggung oleh generasi akan datang.
Oleh itu, PAS perlu menjelaskan dengan terang empat tunggak utama:

• Apakah langkah konkrit yang akan diambil untuk membanteras rasuah? • Apakah mekanisme yang akan digunapakai untuk menutup ruang ketirisan? • Apakah dasar baru yang akan diperkenalkan terhadap sistem perolehan kerajaan? • Apakah tindakan yang akan diambil terhadap mereka yang menyalahgunakan kuasa, termasuk jika mereka datang daripada parti atau gabungan politik sendiri?

Empat persoalan dan jawapan dari pihak PAS ini sangat penting. Rakyat tidak mahu mendengar janji membanteras rasuah hanya ketika PAS menjadi pembangkang. Rakyat mahu melihat apakah prinsip yang sama akan digunakan apabila PAS menjadi kerajaan dan berhadapan dengan pesalah dari orang dalam kalangan mereka sendiri atau rakan politik mereka. Yang salah, tetap salah, sama ada kawan atau lawan.

Berhubung gejala rasuah, kenyataan presiden PAS dimuktamar semalam tidak memberansangkan. Sila lihat 'Corruption in Malaysia weaponised to discredit rivals, claims Hadi'. Apakah kerajaan PAS kelak tidak akan menutup segala kebocoran dan ketirisan dalam sistem kewangan negara?
Jika kebocoran tidak ditutup, berapa banyak pun hasil yang dikutip, negara akan terus menghadapi masalah yang sama, tidak kira pesalahnya menganut agama apa sekalipun.

Ia bukan lagi isu moral semata-mata. Ia adalah isu ekonomi, isu kekuatan kewangan negara dan ianya juga, adalah isu masa depan generasi muda Malaysia. Sebab itu, isu gejala rasuah, ketirisan dan salah guna kuasa amat penting untuk dijadikan landasan sebenar polisi parti dan ia merangkumi sebahagian daripada dasar fiskal dan kewangan negara.
Jadi sebelum PAS meminta rakyat memberikan mandat untuk memimpin Putrajaya, mereka perlu terlebih dahulu menjawab satu soalan yang mudah tetapi sangat besar maknanya:
Apakah sebenarnya rancangan fiskal PAS untuk Malaysia?

3e8a758c7a64ac70: The US military's effort to prevent troops from being tracked by adversaries through purchased location data hasn't worked as well as anticipated, and lawmakers want to know why. US Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) and Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-NC) on Friday asked for an investigation by the Defense Department Inspector General into policies that have only partially stanched the flow of location data that allows military personnel to be tracked and targeted. In May, Wyden, Harrigan, and a bipartisan group of 12 other members of Congress released details about how commercially purchased location data – often captured by mobile apps and advertising SDKs – can be used to identify where US military personnel gather and to target those locations. They noted that the DoD has been aware of this threat since at least 2016. The lawmakers urged Defense Department CIO Kirsten A. Davies to take steps to mitigate this risk, including turning off advertising identifiers on DoD smartphones and issuing a policy requiring the disabling of advertising identifiers on all personal devices brought into DoD facilities or overseas. Since then, various military branches have blocked advertising identifiers on government-issued devices. According to the letter, "several DoD components – the Army, Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and Special Operations Command – confirm that they now disable advertising IDs on government-issued devices to protect their personnel from such threats." But that hasn't entirely eliminated the availability of location data tied to US military personnel. Citing ongoing reports, Wyden and Harrigan want to know why location data pinpointing the movement of troops continues to be available. "We commend these service branches for implementing this cybersecurity defensive best practice on government devices," they said in their letter [PDF] to the DoD IG. "However, recent reports regarding the continued availability of commercial location data originating from DoD facilities raise troubling questions." The two lawmakers speculate about the reason DoD policies have fallen short. One possibility, they say, is that some parts of the DoD turned off their advertising identifiers only as recently as July. Another, they say, is that disabling ad identifiers may no longer be sufficient to limit the availability of location data. And the third is that the location data is coming entirely from the personal devices of DoD personnel and contractors. Zach Edwards, staff threat researcher at Infoblox, told The Register in an email that it's good to hear all the military branches have disabled advertising IDs on their phones because it will make members of the military and their families safer, especially those serving in combat zones overseas. "This change will essentially ensure that military device location data isn't being included in bulk data sales being done by numerous vendors," he said. "It’s truly unfortunate that Google and Apple have not effectively reformed their mobile advertising IDs, even after it’s been well documented that it’s the primary piece of data being used by data brokers to connect up people’s mobile phone location data for bulk sales." Mobile advertising identifiers (MAIDs), Edwards explained, serve as join keys for tracking people – they can link different datasets. "So one core benefit is that military data won't be available for sale via data brokers, who will sell to literally anyone with a pulse and a credit card," said Edwards. "But the other slightly less obvious benefit is that this MAID was also being broadcast to all ad systems participating in the auctions." Edwards said that while states like California, Vermont, Texas, and Oregon have data broker registries, he's unaware of any Russian or Chinese ad tech vendors who have registered. And those companies, he said, partner with Western publishers and mobile apps to collect data anyway. "I think it's important to appreciate that these ad tech companies in Russia and China have also likely been getting MAID data from the programmatic ad tech auctions from members of the military, and companies in those countries have an obligation to share it with the state without any ability to appeal or provide any external notice," he said. ®

dbcf89bb6cac86e8: After nearly eight years, ESA and JAXA's BepiColombo spacecraft is finally nearing Mercury, as engineers begin the arrival sequence by jettisoning the power module that got it this far. The spacecraft stack separated from the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) on September 3 at around 1400 CEST. After a tense few minutes, controllers confirmed that a preliminary Doppler signal had been detected, indicating that the MTM had separated successfully; by 1552 CEST, it was confirmed that signals had been picked up, indicating that all had gone to plan. The solar panels of the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) were charging the spacecraft's batteries. The next stage involves dropping into orbit around Mercury on November 21. Then the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO) – aka Mio – will be released between December 9 and 10, and a week later MPO will start moving to its final orbit over 480 x 1500 km, with science commencing in April 2027. The arrival is a year later than planned. BepiColombo was supposed to have been orbiting Mercury in December 2025, but problems with the spacecraft's Solar Electric Power (SEP) system meant the trajectory had to be rethought, which extended the spacecraft's cruise. BepiColombo is no stranger to Mercury and has performed six flybys of the planet since 2021. It has also conducted flybys of Venus and Earth following its 2018 launch. The spacecraft is an impressive example of international cooperation. The MPO and MTM are ESA contributions, while the MMO comes from JAXA. ESA also provided the sunshield to protect the MMO during transit. This sunshield will be ejected after the MMO is released. The MPO is the big brother of the BepiColombo partnership, with a main body measuring 2.4 x 2.2 x 1.7 m and a mass of 1,230 kg (including an 85 kg science payload). JAXA's MMO is 1.8 m in diameter and 1.1 m high, and weighs 255 kg (45 kg of which is the science payload). While MPO is 3-axis stabilized and nadir-pointing, MMO will be spin-stabilized at 15 rpm, with its spin axis 90 degrees to the Sun. The goal of the mission is a study of Mercury, "from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind, to the properties of its large iron core and the origin of its magnetic field." The initial mission at Mercury is planned for one Earth year (approximately four Mercury years), although it could be extended by another Earth year. ®
